connections.untrained: This task used Google services, whose data goes only to brains that never use it to train AI. Pick one, or add one.
connections.keyHint: Only if the service gave you a key. Otherwise you’ll be asked to sign in.
connections.failed: Couldn’t connect. Check the address: some services don’t accept connections from a browser yet.
connections.needsKey: This service needs you to sign in, or a key.
connections.failedKnown: Couldn’t connect to {service}. Try again in a moment.
gateway.title: Gateway
gateway.text: Some services don’t accept connections from a browser yet. {name} can reach them through a gateway, run by your organization or by you: give its address here.
connections.lede: Each one’s page says what {name} may do there.
connections.needsYou: {service} needs you to sign in again.
connections.usual: Where you choose nothing here, {name} does as Approvals says for every service.
connections.guarded: Approvals holds a stricter rule for {service}, which comes first.
connections.trains: What {service} brings in goes only to brains that never train on it.
connections.disconnectAsk: Disconnect {service}? Its key leaves this device; nothing changes in {service} itself.

connections.laterCount.one: {count} more, not from a browser yet
connections.laterCount.other: {count} more, not from a browser yet

connections.laterText: Through a gateway, run by your organization or by you
connections.otherText: For a service {name} doesn’t list. Its address comes from the service, or from your organization.
connections.signInThere: If {service} asks, you sign in there, then come back here. {name} never sees your password.
connections.sealed: Its key stays on this device, sealed, and never goes into a backup, an export or a share.
connections.another: {service} is connected already: this adds another account.
